Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish mapmaker, trained at Leuven, whose world map of 1569 introduced the projection that bears his name.

On his map, lines of constant compass bearing appear as straight lines, so a sailor could draw a course with a ruler. To do so the map stretches areas away from the equator, which is why Greenland looks as large as Africa. The projection became the standard for sea charts and, much later, for web maps.

Mercator also coined the word atlas for a book of maps. He was jailed for months in 1544 on suspicion of Protestant heresy and later moved to Duisburg in Germany. His work came out of the busy map trade of Antwerp and the age of the great voyages. See Belgium.
sum: Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish mapmaker, trained at Leuven, whose world map of 1569 introduced the projection that bears his name.
